items.title: Frozen in Time: How a Physics Foundation Model Forgets Under Sim-to-Real Adaptation
items.summary: Scientific foundation models face catastrophic forgetting when adapting from simulations to real-world data. Study on a physics foundation model showed that finetuning on simulations rapidly degraded performance on original pretraining tasks. Subsequent adaptation to real data further eroded performance on the simulated task. Replaying just 1% of the simulated data during real-data finetuning helped recover lost simulation performance. The research concludes that lightweight replay strategies are effective for mitigating catastrophic forgetting in sim-to-real adaptation of SciFMs.
items.audio_script: From arXiv - cs.LG, "Frozen in Time: How a Physics Foundation Model Forgets Under Sim-to-Real Adaptation" reports on the challenge of catastrophic forgetting experienced by physics foundation models during the adaptation process from simulations to real-world data. The research demonstrated that finetuning a physics foundation model on simulations led to a rapid degradation of performance on the original pretraining tasks, and subsequent adaptation to real data further reduced performance on the simulated tasks. The study involved applying finetuning techniques to a physics foundation model, observing performance decay, and subsequently testing adaptation methods. The researchers found that replaying only one percent of the simulated data during real-data finetuning was sufficient to recover lost simulation performance. This indicates that lightweight replay strategies are effective for mitigating catastrophic forgetting in the sim-to-real adaptation of scientific foundation models. This development points toward improved stability and efficiency in deploying physics-informed artificial intelligence systems.

items.title: Reliability-Weighted Direct Preference Optimization: Penalized Weights for Robust Preference Learning
items.summary: Reliability-Weighted Direct Preference Optimization (RW-DPO) incorporates an unknown reliability weight for each preference comparison, where a weight of 1 indicates agreement and 0 indicates a reversed comparison. It estimates these weights jointly with the policy using a minimax-concave penalty on the negative log of the weights. This penalty ensures the model agrees with comparisons weighted at 1 and only penalizes contradictions. The method consistently recovers preference directions and weights, even when a fraction of labels are flipped. Simulations show RW-DPO achieves lower estimation error than other robust preference learning methods.
items.audio_script: From arXiv - stat.ML, "Reliability-Weighted Direct Preference Optimization: Penalized Weights for Robust Preference Learning" details a new method for robust preference learning that incorporates unknown reliability weights for preference comparisons. The method estimates these weights jointly with the policy using a minimax-concave penalty on the negative log of the weights to ensure agreement with weighted comparisons while penalizing only contradictions. Simulations demonstrated that this approach consistently recovers preference directions and weights even when a fraction of labels are flipped, achieving lower estimation error than other robust preference learning methods. This research advances the field of preference modeling by introducing a technique for more reliable learning from preference data. The development suggests improved robustness in aligning AI models with human preferences across varied data sets.

items.title: Statistical Foundations of Reinforcement Learning: A Non-Asymptotic Perspective
items.summary: Reinforcement learning requires understanding its statistical foundations, especially concerning data efficiency in sample-starved scenarios. The paper provides a non-asymptotic statistical treatment for RL based on tabular Markov decision processes. It focuses on analyzing three sampling mechanisms—RL with a generative model, online RL, and offline RL—across model-based and model-free paradigms. The research emphasizes minimax-optimal algorithm design and sharp statistical characterizations of various RL algorithms. Extensions to the topic, like robust RL and multi-agent systems, are also briefly discussed.
items.audio_script: From arXiv - stat.ML, "Statistical Foundations of Reinforcement Learning: A Non-Asymptotic Perspective" details a non-asymptotic statistical treatment of reinforcement learning focusing on data efficiency in sample-starved scenarios. The research provides a statistical framework based on tabular Markov decision processes to analyze three sampling mechanisms including reinforcement learning with a generative model, online reinforcement learning, and offline reinforcement learning across model-based and model-free paradigms. The study emphasizes the design of minimax-optimal algorithms and the derivation of sharp statistical characterizations for various reinforcement learning algorithms. Extensions to this work also address robust reinforcement learning and multi-agent systems. This research advances the statistical understanding required for developing more efficient and reliable reinforcement learning systems in practical applications.

items.title: Certified Behavioral Retention for Continual Adaptation with Held-Out Anchors
items.summary: Certified Anchor-Based Adaptation (CABA) is introduced as a candidate-agnostic post-update gate for continual adaptation in machine learning. It reserves historical observations and compares policies on frozen representations to select an update based on a budget constraint. The framework provides a theory-led certification that separates measured anchor retention from conditional off-anchor guarantees. Under specific assumptions, an accepted update guarantees a uniform behavioral-divergence bound on protected support. Experimental results show CABA reduces mean forgetting significantly in a Human Activity Recognition study.
items.audio_script: From arXiv - cs.LG, "Certified Behavioral Retention for Continual Adaptation with Held-Out Anchors" introduces Certified Anchor-Based Adaptation as a candidate-agnostic post-update gate for continual adaptation in machine learning, demonstrating a framework that reserves historical observations to select updates based on a budget constraint. The framework establishes a theory-led certification that distinguishes measured anchor retention from conditional off-anchor guarantees by comparing policies on frozen representations and selecting updates based on these retained observations. Under specific assumptions, an accepted update guarantees a uniform behavioral-divergence bound on protected support, and experimental results from a Human Activity Recognition study indicate that this approach significantly reduces mean forgetting. This research provides a verifiable method for ensuring stable performance during sequential machine learning updates. The findings suggest a path toward more robust and reliably adapting artificial intelligence systems.

items.title: Don't Just Impute, Detect: Task-Aware Diffusion Pipelines for Edge Anomaly Detection
items.summary: Standard edge anomaly detection uses an "impute-then-detect" pipeline where imputation based on Mean Squared Error introduces bias. The proposed Task-Aware Diffusion Refiner (TADR) addresses this by conditioning the diffusion refinement on a frozen downstream detector's loss landscape. This method improves anomaly detection by $\text{F1}$ by $0.338$ over unrefined detectors on SMD. TADR's benefit is shown to correlate with available redundant channels and the anomaly evidence removed by the outage. The method is computationally efficient, running quickly on a single CPU core.
items.audio_script: From arXiv - cs.LG, "Don't Just Impute, Detect: Task-Aware Diffusion Pipelines for Edge Anomaly Detection" reports on a method for improving edge anomaly detection. The research introduces the Task-Aware Diffusion Refiner which addresses bias introduced by standard imputation methods in anomaly detection pipelines. The methodology involves conditioning the diffusion refinement process on the loss landscape of a frozen downstream detector. This approach improves anomaly detection performance by a factor of zero point three three eight over unrefined detectors on SMD. The method demonstrates a correlation with the presence of redundant channels and the anomaly evidence removed by an outage, while remaining computationally efficient for execution on a single CPU core. This advancement indicates a path toward more accurate and efficient anomaly detection systems in resource-constrained environments.

items.title: Automatic Construction of Strong Simple Baselines
items.summary: The research investigates using large language models to automatically construct strong, simple baselines for deep learning methods in scientific applications. This was achieved by assembling 36 supervised classification and regression tasks from peer-reviewed literature in high-impact journals. The automatically generated baselines were found to recover a median of 95.5% of the performance gap between trivial predictors and deep learning models. These simple baselines often matched or exceeded the performance of the deep learning models in 12 studies. The findings suggest that automated baseline construction is a practical method for assessing deep learning contributions in the physical and life sciences.
items.audio_script: From arXiv - cs.LG, "Automatic Construction of Strong Simple Baselines" investigates the use of large language models to automatically construct strong, simple baselines for deep learning methods in scientific applications, achieving a median recovery of 95.5% of the performance gap. The research involved assembling thirty-six supervised classification and regression tasks drawn from peer-reviewed literature in high-impact journals to train the large language models. These models were utilized to automatically generate simple baselines. The results indicated that these automatically constructed baselines often matched or exceeded the performance of the deep learning models in twelve separate studies. This suggests that automated baseline construction is a practical methodology for assessing the contribution of deep learning in the physical and life sciences. The findings indicate a viable method for benchmarking deep learning advancements in scientific domains.

items.title: Coarse-Graining Optimal Transport for Rollout-Free Post-Training of Flow Matching
items.summary: Flow matching's performance depends on the coupling used to pair source and target samples, but practical limitations hinder consistently improving sampling quality via optimal transport. ReCouple is introduced as a framework to construct coarse-grained optimal transport couplings for rollout-free post-training. Extensions, ReCouple+ and ReCouple++, further address continuous source settings and spatial regularization, respectively. Empirical results show that the interplay between coupling optimality, neural realizability, and generation quality is dependent on the number of function evaluations. These methods effectively reveal the complex relationship governing post-training in flow matching.
items.audio_script: From arXiv - stat.ML, "Coarse-Graining Optimal Transport for Rollout-Free Post-Training of Flow Matching" details a framework for improving the sampling quality in flow matching through coarse-grained optimal transport. The research introduces ReCouple, a framework designed to construct coarse-grained optimal transport couplings for rollout-free post-training. Extensions, ReCouple+ and ReCouple++, further address continuous source settings and spatial regularization, respectively. Empirical results indicate that the interplay between coupling optimality, neural realizability, and generation quality is dependent on the number of function evaluations. These methods effectively reveal the complex relationship governing post-training in flow matching. This work provides a method for enhancing the quality of generative models in flow matching systems.

items.title: CausalGrade: Evidence-Guided Causal Graph Scoring with Jev
items.summary: CausalGrade is a method for scoring the structural quality of candidate causal graphs by integrating evidence-guided scoring with the probabilistic judgment model Jev. It incorporates evidence of association, conditional dependence, and directionality from observational data and edge probabilities derived from a causal discovery foundation model. Jev generates probabilistic judgments about direct causal edges, and the final graph score measures the agreement between the evaluated graph's structure and these edge-level judgments. Testing on synthetic datasets showed that higher scores correlate with smaller structural errors across various causal discovery algorithms. CausalGrade achieved a 54.4\% best-candidate hit rate in graph selection tasks, outperforming the Self-Compatibility metric.
items.audio_script: From arXiv - stat.ML, "CausalGrade: Evidence-Guided Causal Graph Scoring with Jev" reports on a method for scoring the structural quality of candidate causal graphs by integrating evidence-guided scoring with the probabilistic judgment model Jev, achieving a 54.4% best-candidate hit rate in graph selection tasks. The method incorporates evidence of association, conditional dependence, and directionality derived from observational data and edge probabilities from a causal discovery foundation model. Jev generates probabilistic judgments regarding direct causal edges, and the final graph score is calculated by measuring the agreement between the evaluated graph's structure and these edge-level judgments. Testing on synthetic datasets indicated that higher scores corresponded with reduced structural errors across various causal discovery algorithms. This development suggests a refined approach for assessing the reliability of inferred causal structures in machine learning applications.

items.title: Near-Optimal First-Order Regret for Bandits with Feedback Graphs
items.summary: The paper studies first-order regret guarantees for adversarial bandits with a fixed, known directed feedback graph. It bridges a gap between existing bounds by obtaining an expected regret bound of $\widetilde{O}(\sqrt{\alpha L^\star}+\alpha)$. The work introduces an algorithm for self-aware graphs by combining EXP3 with a sampling rule from exploration by optimization. This involves constructing a map whose fixed points control the one-round regret remainder using the graph's independence number. Finally, the algorithm is extended to general strongly observable graphs, achieving the same guarantee through adaptation of the two-level aggregation approach.
items.audio_script: From arXiv - cs.LG, "Near-Optimal First-Order Regret for Bandits with Feedback Graphs" studies first-order regret guarantees for adversarial bandits with a fixed, known directed feedback graph, yielding an expected regret bound of $\widetilde{O}(\sqrt{\alpha L^\star}+\alpha)$. The research introduces an algorithm for self-aware graphs by combining EXP3 with a sampling rule from exploration by optimization. This methodology involves constructing a map whose fixed points control the one-round regret remainder utilizing the graph's independence number. Furthermore, the algorithm is extended to general strongly observable graphs, achieving the same regret guarantee through adaptation of the two-level aggregation approach. This work advances the theoretical understanding of exploration strategies in sequential decision-making under graph constraints. Future developments will focus on applying these bounds to complex, real-world machine learning problems.

items.title: AutoHebb: Self-Modifying Neural Networks that Zero-Shot Infer and Continually Learn
items.summary: AutoHebb introduces self-modifying Hebbian networks designed to achieve zero-shot inference and continual learning. These networks autonomously combine external feedback with internal activity to generate a global learning signal, or 'neuromodulator'. This neuromodulator gates a biologically grounded local learning rule, based on the 3-factor Hebbian rule, which updates the network's weights. Meta-learning for fixed weights allows AutoHebb networks to excel on zero-shot tasks and exhibit emergent ZI/CL abilities. The research suggests meta-learning, Hebbian plasticity, and autonomous control are essential for these learning capabilities.
items.audio_script: From arXiv - cs.LG, "AutoHebb: Self-Modifying Neural Networks that Zero-Shot Infer and Continually Learn" details a method for creating self-modifying Hebbian networks capable of zero-shot inference and continual learning. The research introduces AutoHebb networks that autonomously combine external feedback and internal activity to generate a global learning signal termed a neuromodulator. This neuromodulator gates a biologically grounded local learning rule based on the three-factor Hebbian rule, which updates the network's weights. Meta-learning applied to fixed weights allows these networks to perform well on zero-shot tasks, demonstrating emergent zero-shot inference and continual learning abilities through the interplay of meta-learning, Hebbian plasticity, and autonomous control. This work indicates a path toward more adaptive and continuously learning artificial intelligence systems.

items.title: INLA for Adaptive UAV Sampling of Radio Environment Maps in IoT Networks: Prior Width Governs Accuracy and Calibration
items.summary: The research uses Integrated Nested Laplace Approximation (INLA) to adaptively sample radio environment maps from non-Gaussian IoT observations using UAVs. Waypoints are selected based on entropy pre-screening and Sherman--Morrison lookahead over the reachable set. Widening the prior shadowing standard deviation from 6.0 to 10.025 dB improved the noise margin and credible-interval coverage. The study shows substantial corpus-dependent sensitivity to prior specification, suggesting the preferred width depends on the data and model mismatch. Overall, prior specification significantly impacts the accuracy and calibration of the adaptive sampling process.

items.title: Robust-by-Design Distributional Learning from Contaminated Samples
items.summary: Data analysis often involves datasets contaminated by unknown mixtures from data collection processes. Standard distributional learning methods either ignore this contamination or discard most of the data when dealing with such samples. The proposed method, CC-MMD, is a design-based estimator that corrects for contamination by combining proxy scores with audited residual corrections. This approach recovers the true maximum mean discrepancy (MMD) from the clean latent sample despite noisy supervision. Empirically, CC-MMD successfully improves parameter recovery and enables generative models trained on corrupted mixtures to learn the clean target distribution.

items.title: The Geometry of Multitask Learning: Sharp Rates for Shared Subspace Estimation
items.summary: A general multitask lemma is proposed to provide sufficient conditions for fast shared subspace estimation in multitask learning. This lemma is based on geometric conditions concerning task regression functions and their estimators. The lemma is used to establish sharp minimax rates for linear regression and classification in relevant settings. Furthermore, the work demonstrates rates matching up to logarithmic factors for additive-noise regression. These results fill a gap in the literature regarding the estimation of shared subspaces in multitask scenarios.

items.title: Adaptive Uncertainty Quantification on Simplicial Complexes with Conformalized Simplicial Neural Networks
items.summary: Simplicial neural networks (SNNs) require rigorous uncertainty quantification (UQ), which they typically lack, limiting their application in sensitive scenarios. The proposed framework, conformalized SNN (CF-SNN), generates prediction sets for multiple targets simultaneously on simplicial complexes. CF-SNN ensures that each target's prediction set includes the true label with a specified nominal coverage probability. Furthermore, the overall miscoverage proportion across all targets is guaranteed to stay close to the nominal level with high probability. Experiments confirm that CF-SNN is a flexible UQ method that provides informative, small-sized prediction sets.

items.title: Conditional Neural SDEs for Financial Time-Series Generation
items.summary: Conditional Neural SDEs are proposed for generating financial time-series paths by combining continuous-time stochastic dynamics with learnable drift and diffusion functions. A residual anchor architecture decomposes the target into a learned conditional anchor and a stochastic residual to improve stability. This approach models the residual dynamics around the anchor, which captures the context-dependent baseline. Evaluation on real-world financial data demonstrates the model's ability to generate plausible paths with competitive accuracy and calibrated uncertainty estimates.

items.title: PDE-Residual-Informed Kriging
items.summary: The study proposes PDE-residual-informed Kriging (PRIK) to incorporate global PDE-residual information directly into the Gaussian process covariance structure. This is an advancement over existing methods that use pointwise conditioning or residual penalties separately. The PRIK method constructs a PDE-residual kernel using the $L^2$ inner product of PDE residuals to minimize the integrated squared PDE residual in the posterior mean. Statistical interpretations show the variance-scale estimate equals the normalized PDE-residual energy, and theoretical results establish convergence rates and bounds for the posterior mean. Numerical experiments confirm the PDE-solving capability of PRIK.

items.title: Unsupervised Feature Selection Using Local Intrinsic Dimensionality -- Extended Version
items.summary: The LIDFS method proposes an unsupervised feature selection technique based on Local Intrinsic Dimensionality (LID) to address dimensionality reduction without class labels. It estimates the LID for each feature based on the distances to its $k$ nearest neighbors to determine local discriminability. Features with lower LID are deemed more important, and a refinement step removes locally redundant features. This method achieves a complete ranking allowing feature selection without further computation, running in $\mathcal{O}(d^2 n)$ time. Evaluation on benchmark datasets shows LIDFS outperforms other methods in both supervised and clustering-based assessments.

items.title: TensorSSM: Memorizing Spatial Position in Dynamic State Space for Tensor Core Generation
items.summary: TensorSSM is a novel Implicit Neural Representation method for functional tensor decomposition that memorizes spatial positions within a dynamic State Space Model (SSM). It decomposes mode-wise coordinates into sequences using a K-ary rule to encode spatial tokens from coarse to fine. The method extends the SSM state space to explicitly map cross-mode spatial dependencies, allowing inter-mode interactions to enhance updates. This integration of spatial information into the state space and tensor core significantly advances state adaptability and expressiveness. Experiments show TensorSSM achieves high reconstruction accuracy and storage efficiency across diverse tensor datasets.

items.title: Bayesian Distribution System State Estimation with Flow Matching
items.summary: The proposed method, PoSE, estimates the state of a distribution system by learning the distribution of substation injections using a neural network trained with flow matching. This approach maintains the Bayesian structure of state estimation, learning only the unknown distribution rather than approximating power flow directly. The power flow equations are incorporated only during sampling via a noise-aware Kalman-type correction. Experiments show PoSE reduces probabilistic injection error significantly compared to Gaussian priors and supervised deep learning estimators. The method achieves this accuracy while providing reliable uncertainty estimates for system states.

items.title: FARO: Function-Space Adaptive Return-to-Risk Optimization via Cross-Block Equal-Risk-Contribution Budget Allocation
items.summary: FARO is a function-space adaptive optimizer that determines parameter block partitioning as its primary decision unit. It assigns geometry to each block based on its counterfactual return and then reallocates a shared budget using cross-block equal-risk contribution. This method successfully recovers human priors in a GPT-style model without manual per-layer geometry setting. Furthermore, the FARO-ERC approach reduces clean-data loss by an average of 0.0136 nats across different seeds. The technique proves robust by trimming riskiest blocks and maintaining performance under corrupted input streams.
